profile.summary: Stack is a single-cell foundation model that reads a set of cells from one sample together, so each cell's representation is informed by the other cells in its context. It takes cell-by-gene count matrices and outputs cell embeddings; through in-context learning it can also generate expression profiles for a target cell population under a condition shown by unlabelled prompt cells, such as a drug or a different donor.

summary_quotes.text: leverages tabular attention to generate representations for each cell informed by the cells in its context
setting cell-by-gene matrix chunks as the basic input data unit

can perform in-context learning from unlabeled cells representing arbitrary conditions, such as a chemical perturbation or a different donor, and predict the effect of those conditions on a target cell population

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Stack is an encoder-decoder with tabular attention: layers alternate between attention across cells and attention across genes. Genes are compressed into a small number of trainable gene-group tokens (100 by default), and the input is a cell set drawn from a single experimental sample. Pre-training uses a rectangular mask: a random list of genes is masked for all cells in a mini-batch, with a mask ratio sampled between 0.1 and 0.8, and the model reconstructs each cell's expression distribution. A post-training stage uses a frozen teacher (self-distillation) so the student learns to predict target cell distributions conditioned on prompt cells.
sections.source_locator: Paper Results and Methods; README.md: Model Architecture

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two checkpoints are on Hugging Face. Stack-Large (bc_large.ckpt) is pre-trained on human scBaseCount for 10 epochs and has 217M parameters according to its card; the card points to the embedding tutorial. Stack-Large-Aligned (bc_large_aligned.ckpt) adds alignment on CellxGene 45M and Parse 10M PBMC for 8 epochs and points to the prediction tutorial. The paper reports configurations from 69 to 629 million parameters. A result should name the checkpoint file and Hugging Face revision.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Encoder-decoder single-cell foundation model with in-context learning over cell sets.

quotes.text: Stack is a large-scale encoder-decoder foundation model

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Tabular attention alternating cell-wise and gene-wise layers; token dimension 16 and hidden (gene-reduction) dimension 100 by default.

quotes.text: **Tabular Attention**: Alternating cell-wise and gene-wise attention layers

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A cell set (cell-by-gene count matrix chunk) from one sample, as an h5ad file, restricted to a gene list; for generation, base and test AnnData files.

quotes.text: is a collection of cells, or a

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Cell embeddings written to an h5ad file; generated cell profiles for a target population in new contexts.
facts.source_locator: README.md: Extracting Stack Embeddings, In-Context Generation

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 217M (Stack-Large and Stack-Large-Aligned, per their model cards). The paper's scaling study spans 69 to 629 million parameters.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Human scBaseCount: 189 million cells after quality control, of which 149 million cells from 19,978 SRX samples formed the training set, with the remaining 20% held out for validation and testing (paper Results). The README and model card give about 150 million. Alignment for Stack-Large-Aligned used CellxGene 45M and Parse 10M PBMC.

quotes.text: trained on 150 million uniformly-preprocessed single cells
a foundation model trained on 149 million uniformly preprocessed human single cells
the largest available human single-cell data collection that contains 189 million cells after strict quality control
The training dataset comprised 19,978 SRX samples and 149 million cells, with the remaining 20% of the data held out for validation and testing

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Stack-Large and Stack-Large-Aligned on Hugging Face.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 256 cells per set optimised validation loss in the paper's scaling tests; no fixed limit is stated. The README's training example uses --sample_size 256 and the fine-tuning example 512.

steps.title: Download the model
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

repo_id = "arcinstitute/Stack-Large"
local_dir = "Stack-Large"
snapshot_download(repo_id=repo_id, repo_type="model", local_dir=local_dir)
EOF

steps.title: Extract embeddings
steps.explanation: The README's embedding command. Replace the checkpoint path with the downloaded checkpoint (Stack-Large holds bc_large.ckpt), data.h5ad with your data and hvg_genes.pkl with the gene list; the sources do not say which file to use as the gene list.
